Warp, the intelligent terminal
Available on MacOS, Linux, Windows ## Features * Statistical analysis across multiple runs. * Support for arbitrary shell commands. * Constant feedback about the benchmark progress and current estimates. * Warmup runs can be executed before the actual benchmark. * Cache-clearing commands can be set up before each timing run. * Statistical outlier detection to detect interference from other programs and caching effects. * Export results to various formats: CSV, JSON, Markdown, AsciiDoc. * Parameterized benchmarks (e.g. vary the number of threads). * Cross-platform ## Usage ### Basic benchmarks To run a benchmark, you can simply call `hyperfine ...`. The argument(s) can be any shell command. For example: ```sh hyperfine 'sleep 0.3' ``` Hyperfine will automatically determine the number of runs to perform for each command. By default, it will perform *at least* 10 benchmarking runs and measure for at least 3 seconds. To change this, you can use the `-r`/`--runs` option: ```sh hyperfine --runs 5 'sleep 0.3' ``` If you want to compare the runtimes of different programs, you can pass multiple commands: ```sh hyperfine 'hexdump file' 'xxd file' ``` ### Warmup runs and preparation commands For programs that perform a lot of disk I/O, the benchmarking results can be heavily influenced by disk caches and whether they are cold or warm. If you want to run the benchmark on a warm cache, you can use the `-w`/`--warmup` option to perform a certain number of program executions before the actual benchmark: ```sh hyperfine --warmup 3 'grep -R TODO *' ``` Conversely, if you want to run the benchmark for a cold cache, you can use the `-p`/`--prepare` option to run a special command before *each* timing run. For example, to clear harddisk caches on Linux, you can run ```sh sync; echo 3 | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches ``` To use this specific command with hyperfine, call `sudo -v` to temporarily gain sudo permissions and then call: ```sh hyperfine --prepare 'sync; echo 3 | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches' 'grep -R TODO *' ``` ### Parameterized benchmarks If you want to run a series of benchmarks where a single parameter is varied (say, the number of threads), you can use the `-P`/`--parameter-scan` option and call: ```sh hyperfine --prepare 'make clean' --parameter-scan num_threads 1 12 'make -j {num_threads}' ``` This also works with decimal numbers. The `-D`/`--parameter-step-size` option can be used to control the step size: ```sh hyperfine --parameter-scan delay 0.3 0.7 -D 0.2 'sleep {delay}' ``` This runs `sleep 0.3`, `sleep 0.5` and `sleep 0.7`. For non-numeric parameters, you can also supply a list of values with the `-L`/`--parameter-list` option: ``` hyperfine -L compiler gcc,clang '{compiler} -O2 main.cpp' ``` ### Intermediate shell By default, commands are executed using a predefined shell (`/bin/sh` on Unix, `cmd.exe` on Windows). If you want to use a different shell, you can use the `-S, --shell ` option: ```sh hyperfine --shell zsh 'for i in {1..10000}; do echo test; done' ``` Note that hyperfine always *corrects for the shell spawning time*. To do this, it performs a calibration procedure where it runs the shell with an empty command (multiple times), to measure the startup time of the shell. It will then subtract this time from the total to show the actual time used by the command in question. If you want to run a benchmark *without an intermediate shell*, you can use the `-N` or `--shell=none` option. This is helpful for very fast commands (< 5 ms) where the shell startup overhead correction would produce a significant amount of noise. Note that you cannot use shell syntax like `*` or `~` in this case. ``` hyperfine -N 'grep TODO /home/user' ``` ### Shell functions and aliases If you are using bash, you can export shell functions to directly benchmark them with hyperfine: ```bash my_function() { sleep 1; } export -f my_function hyperfine --shell=bash my_function ``` Otherwise, inline them into or source them from the benchmarked progr 7201 characters elided option: ```sh hyperfine --shell zsh 'for i in {1..10000}; do echo test; done' ``` Note that hyperfine always *corrects for the shell spawning time*. This option affects the standard output as well as all export formats
except for CSV and JSON.
.HP
\fB\-\-export\-asciidoc\fR \fIFILE\fP 
.IP
Export the timing summary statistics as an AsciiDoc table to the given \fIFILE\fP.
The output time unit can be changed using the \fB\-\-time\-unit\fR option.
.HP
\fB\-\-export\-csv\fR \fIFILE\fP
.IP
Export the timing summary statistics as CSV to the given \fIFILE\fP. If you need the
timing results for each individual run, use the JSON export format.
The output time unit is always seconds.
.HP
\fB\-\-export\-json\fR \fIFILE\fP
.IP
Export the timing summary statistics and timings of individual runs as JSON to
the given \fIFILE\fP. The output time unit is always seconds.
.HP
\fB\-\-export\-markdown\fR \fIFILE\fP
.IP
Export the timing summary statistics as a Markdown table to the given \fIFILE\fP.
The output time unit can be changed using the \fB\-\-time\-unit\fR option.
.HP
\fB\-\-export\-orgmode\fR \fIFILE\fP
.IP
Export the timing summary statistics as an Emacs org\-mode table to the
given \fIFILE\fP. The output time unit can be changed using the \fB\-\-time\-unit\fR option.
.HP
\fB\-\-show\-output\fR
.IP
Print the stdout and stderr of the benchmark instead of suppressing it. This
will increase the time it takes for benchmarks to run, so it should only be
used for debugging purposes or when trying to benchmark output speed.
.HP
\fB\-\-output\fR \fIWHERE\fP
.IP
Control where the output of the benchmark is redirected. Note that
some programs like 'grep' detect when standard output is \fI\,/dev/null\/\fP and
apply certain optimizations. To avoid that, consider using
\-\-output=pipe.
.IP
\fIWHERE\fP can be:
.RS
.IP null
Redirect output to \fI\,/dev/null\/\fP (the default).
.IP pipe
Feed the output through a pipe before discarding it.
.IP inherit
Don't redirect the output at all (same as \&'\-\-show\-output').
.IP "<FILE>"
Write the output to the given file.
.RE
.IP
This option can be specified once for all commands or multiple times,
once for each command. Note: If you want to log the output of each and
every iteration, you can use a shell redirection and the $HYPERFINE_ITERATION
environment variable: 'my-command > output-${HYPERFINE_ITERATION}.log'
.HP
\fB\-\-input\fR \fIWHERE\fP
.IP
Control where the input of the benchmark comes from.
.IP
\fIWHERE\fP can be:
.RS
.IP null
Read from \fI\,/dev/null\/\fP (the default).
.IP "<FILE>"
Read the input from the given file.
.RE
.HP
\fB\-n\fR, \fB\-\-command\-name\fR \fiNAME\fP
.IP
Give a meaningful \fiNAME\fP to a command. This can be specified multiple times
if several commands are benchmarked.
.HP
\fB\-h\fR, \fB\-\-help\fR
.IP
Print help
.HP
\fB\-V\fR, \fB\-\-version\fR
.IP
Print version
.SH EXAMPLES
.LP
Basic benchmark of 'find . -name todo.txt':
.RS
.nf
\fBhyperfine\fR 'find . -name todo.txt'
.fi
.RE
.LP
Perform benchmarks for 'sleep 0.2' and 'sleep 3.2' with a minimum 5 runs each:
.RS
.nf
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-\-min\-runs\fR 5 'sleep 0.2' 'sleep 3.2'
.fi
.RE
.LP
Perform a benchmark of 'grep' with a warm disk cache by executing 3 runs up front that are not part
of the measurement: 
.RS
.nf
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-\-warmup\fR 3 'grep -R TODO *'
.fi
.RE
.LP
Export the results of a parameter scan benchmark to a markdown table: 
.RS
.nf
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-\-export\-markdown\fR output.md \fB\-\-parameter-scan\fR time 1 5 'sleep {time}'
.fi
.RE
.LP
Demonstrate when each of \fB\-\-setup\fR, \fB\-\-prepare\fR, \fB\-\-conclude\fR, \fIcmd\fP and \fB\-\-cleanup\fR will run:
.RS
.nf
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-L\fR n 1,2 \fB\-r\fR 2 \fB\-\-show-output\fR \\
	\fB\-\-setup\fR 'echo setup n={n}' \\
	\fB\-\-prepare\fR 'echo prepare={n}' \\
	\fB\-\-conclude\fR 'echo conclude={n}' \\
	\fB\-\-cleanup\fR 'echo cleanup n={n}' \\
	'echo command n={n}'
.fi
.RE
.RE
.SH AUTHOR
.LP
David Peter <mail@david-peter.de>
.LP
Source, bug tracker, and additional information can be found on GitHub:
.I https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine

          explicitly disabled via '--shell=none'. If multiple commands are
          given, hyperfine will show a comparison of the respective runtimes.

Options:
  -w, --warmup <NUM>
          Perform NUM warmup runs before the actual benchmark. This can be used
          to fill (disk) caches for I/O-heavy programs.
  -m, --min-runs <NUM>
          Perform at least NUM runs for each command (default: 10).
  -M, --max-runs <NUM>
          Perform at most NUM runs for each command. By default, there is no
          limit.
  -r, --runs <NUM>
          Perform exactly NUM runs for each command. If this option is not
          specified, hyperfine automatically determines the number of runs.
  -s, --setup <CMD>
          Execute CMD before each set of timing runs. This is useful for
          compiling your software with the provided parameters, or to do any
          other work that should happen once before a series of benchmark runs,
          not every time as would happen with the --prepare option.
      --reference <CMD>
          The reference command for the relative comparison of results. If this
          is unset, results are compared with the fastest command as reference.
      --reference-name <CMD>
          Give a meaningful name to the reference command.
  -p, --prepare <CMD>
          Execute CMD before each timing run. This is useful for clearing disk
          caches, for example.
          The --prepare option can be specified once for all commands or
          multiple times, once for each command. In the latter case, each
          preparation command will be run prior to the corresponding benchmark
          command.
  -C, --conclude <CMD>
          Execute CMD after each timing run. This is useful for killing
          long-running processes started (e.g. a web server started in
          --prepare), for example.
          The --conclude option can be specified once for all commands or
          multiple times, once for each command. In the latter case, each
          conclude command will be run after the corresponding benchmark
          command.
  -c, --cleanup <CMD>
          Execute CMD after the completion of all benchmarking runs for each
          individual command to be benchmarked. This is useful if the commands
          to be benchmarked produce artifacts that need to be cleaned up.
  -P, --parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>
          Perform benchmark runs for each value in the range MIN..MAX. Replaces
          the string '{VAR}' in each command by the current parameter value.
          
            Example:  hyperfine -P threads 1 8 'make -j {threads}'
          
          This performs benchmarks for 'make -j 1', 'make -j 2', …, 'make -j 8'.
          
          To have the value increase following different patterns, use shell
          arithmetics.
          
            Example: hyperfine -P size 0 3 'sleep $((2**{size}))'
          
          This performs benchmarks with power of 2 increases: 'sleep 1', 'sleep
          2', 'sleep 4', …
          The exact syntax may vary depending on your shell and OS.
  -D, --parameter-step-size <DELTA>
          This argument requires --parameter-scan to be specified as well.
          Traverse the range MIN..MAX in steps of DELTA.
          
            Example:  hyperfine -P delay 0.3 0.7 -D 0.2 'sleep {delay}'
          
          This performs benchmarks for 'sleep 0.3', 'sleep 0.5' and 'sleep 0.7'.
  -L, --parameter-list <VAR> <VALUES>
          Perform benchmark runs for each value in the comma-separated list
          VALUES. Replaces the string '{VAR}' in each command by the current
          parameter value.
          
          Example:  hyperfine -L compiler gcc,clang '{compiler} -O2 main.cpp'
          
          This performs benchmarks for 'gcc -O2 main.cpp' and 'clang -O2
          main.cpp'.
          
          The option can be specified multiple times to run benchmarks for all
          possible parameter combinations.
  -S, --shell <SHELL>
          Set the shell to use for executing benchmarked commands. This can be
          the name or the path to the shell executable, or a full command line
          like "bash --norc". It can also be set to "default" to explicitly
          select the default shell on this platform. Finally, this can also be
          set to "none" to disable the shell. In this case, commands will be
          executed directly. They can still have arguments, but more complex
          things like "sleep 0.1; sleep 0.2" are not possible without a shell.
  -N
          An alias for '--shell=none'.
  -i, --ignore-failure[=<MODE>]
          Ignore failures of the benchmarked programs. Without a value or with
          'all-non-zero', all non-zero exit codes are ignored. You can also
          provide a comma-separated list of exit codes to ignore (e.g.,
          --ignore-failure=1,2).
      --style <TYPE>

          output coloring and interactive elements. Set it to 'full' to enable
          all effects even if no interactive terminal was detected. Set this to
          'nocolor' to keep the interactive output without any colors. Set this
          to 'color' to keep the colors without any interactive output. Set this
          to 'none' to disable all the output of the tool.
      --sort <METHOD>
          Specify the sort order of the speed comparison summary and the
          exported tables for markup formats (Markdown, AsciiDoc, org-mode):
            * 'auto' (default): the speed comparison will be ordered by time and
              the markup tables will be ordered by command (input order).
            * 'command': order benchmarks in the way they were specified
            * 'mean-time': order benchmarks by mean runtime
  -u, --time-unit <UNIT>
          Set the time unit to be used. Possible values: microsecond,
          millisecond, second. If the option is not given, the time unit is
          determined automatically. This option affects the standard output as
          well as all export formats except for CSV and JSON.
      --export-asciidoc <FILE>

          FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit

      --export-csv <FILE>

      --export-json <FILE>

      --export-markdown <FILE>

          FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit

      --export-orgmode <FILE>

          given FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit
          option.
      --show-output

          should only be used for debugging purposes or when trying to benchmark
          output speed.

#!/usr/bin/env python3

Usage: executable [OPTIONS] <command>...

Arguments:
  <command>...
          The command to benchmark. This can be the name of an executable, a
          command line like "grep -i todo" or a shell command like "sleep 0.5 &&
          echo test". The latter is only available if the shell is not
          explicitly disabled via '--shell=none'. If multiple commands are
          given, hyperfine will show a comparison of the respective runtimes.

Options:
  -w, --warmup <NUM>
          Perform NUM warmup runs before the actual benchmark. This can be used
          to fill (disk) caches for I/O-heavy programs.
  -m, --min-runs <NUM>
          Perform at least NUM runs for each command (default: 10).
  -M, --max-runs <NUM>
          Perform at most NUM runs for each command. By default, there is no
          limit.
  -r, --runs <NUM>
          Perform exactly NUM runs for each command. If this option is not
          specified, hyperfine automatically determines the number of runs.
  -s, --setup <CMD>
          Execute CMD before each set of timing runs. This is useful for
          compiling your software with the provided parameters, or to do any
          other work that should happen once before a series of benchmark runs,
          not every time as would happen with the --prepare option.
      --reference <CMD>
          The reference command for the relative comparison of results. If this
          is unset, results are compared with the fastest command as reference.
      --reference-name <CMD>
          Give a meaningful name to the reference command.
  -p, --prepare <CMD>
          Execute CMD before each timing run. This is useful for clearing disk
          caches, for example.
          The --prepare option can be specified once for all commands or
          multiple times, once for each command. In the latter case, each
          preparation command will be run prior to the corresponding benchmark
          command.
  -C, --conclude <CMD>
          Execute CMD after each timing run. This is useful for killing
          long-running processes started (e.g. a web server started in
          --prepare), for example.
          The --conclude option can be specified once for all commands or
          multiple times, once for each command. In the latter case, each
          conclude command will be run after the corresponding benchmark
          command.
  -c, --cleanup <CMD>
          Execute CMD after the completion of all benchmarking runs for each
          individual command to be benchmarked. This is useful if the commands
          to be benchmarked produce artifacts that need to be cleaned up.
  -P, --parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>
          Perform benchmark runs for each value in the range MIN..MAX. Replaces
          the string '{VAR}' in each command by the current parameter value.
          
            Example:  hyperfine -P threads 1 8 'make -j {threads}'
          
          This performs benchmarks for 'make -j 1', 'make -j 2', …, 'make -j 8'.
          
          To have the value increase following different patterns, use shell
          arithmetics.
          
            Example: hyperfine -P size 0 3 'sleep $((2**{size}))'
          
          This performs benchmarks for 'sleep 1', 'sleep 2', 'sleep 4', …
          The exact syntax may vary depending on your shell and OS.
  -D, --parameter-step-size <DELTA>
          This argument requires --parameter-scan to be specified as well.
          Traverse the range MIN..MAX in steps of DELTA.
          
            Example:  hyperfine -P delay 0.3 0.7 -D 0.2 'sleep {delay}'
          
          This performs benchmarks for 'sleep 0.3', 'sleep 0.5' and 'sleep 0.7'.
  -L, --parameter-list <VAR> <VALUES>
          Perform benchmark runs for each value in the comma-separated list
          VALUES. Replaces the string '{VAR}' in each command by the current
          parameter value.
          
          Example:  hyperfine -L compiler gcc,clang '{compiler} -O2 main.cpp'
          
          This performs benchmarks for 'gcc -O2 main.cpp' and 'clang -O2
          main.cpp'.
          
          The option can be specified multiple times to run benchmarks for all
          possible parameter combinations.
  -S, --shell <SHELL>
          Set the shell to use for executing benchmarked commands. This can be
          the name or the path to the shell executable, or a full command line
          like "bash --norc". It can also be set to "default" to explicitly
          select the default shell on this platform. Finally, this can also be
          set to "none" to disable the shell. In this case, commands will be

          well as all export formats except for CSV and JSON.
      --export-asciidoc <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as an AsciiDoc table to the given
          FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit
          option.
      --export-csv <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as CSV to the given FILE. If you
          need the timing results for each individual run, use the JSON export
          format. The output time unit is always seconds.
      --export-json <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics and timings of individual runs as
          JSON to the given FILE. The output time unit is always seconds
      --export-markdown <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as a Markdown table to the given
          FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit
          option.
      --export-orgmode <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as an Emacs org-mode table to the
          given FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit
          option.
      --show-output
          Print the stdout and stderr of the benchmark instead of suppressing
          it. This will increase the time it takes for benchmarks to run, so it
          should only be used for debugging purposes or when trying to benchmark
          output speed.
      --output <WHERE>
          Control where the output of the benchmark is redirected. Note that
          some programs like 'grep' detect when standard output is /dev/null and
          apply certain optimizations. To avoid that, consider using
          '--output=pipe'.
          
          <WHERE> can be:
          
            null:     Redirect output to /dev/null (the default).
          
            pipe:     Feed the output through a pipe before discarding it.
          
            inherit:  Don't redirect the output at all (same as
            '--show-output').
          
            <FILE>:   Write the output to the given file.
          
          This option can be specified once for all commands or multiple times,
          once for each command. Note: If you want to log the output of each and
          every iteration, you can use a shell redirection and the
          '$HYPERFINE_ITERATION' environment variable:
              hyperfine 'my-command > output-${HYPERFINE_ITERATION}.log'
      --input <WHERE>
          Control where the input of the benchmark comes from.
          
          <WHERE> can be:
          
            null:     Read from /dev/null (the default).
          
            <FILE>:   Read the input from the given file.
  -n, --command-name <NAME>
          Give a meaningful name to a command. This can be specified multiple
          times if several commands are benchmarked.
  -h, --help
          Print help
  -V, --version
          Print version
"""

VERSION = "hyperfine 1.20.0"

def eprint(msg, end="\n"):
    sys.stderr.write(msg + ("" if msg.endswith("\n") else end))

def error_clap(msg, usage="executable [OPTIONS] <command>..."):
    sys.stderr.write(f"error: {msg}\n\nUsage: {usage}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
    sys.exit(2)

def error_runtime(msg):
    sys.stderr.write(f"Error: {msg}\n")
    sys.exit(1)

def parse_int_arg(name, value):
    try:
        return int(value)
    except:
        error_runtime(f"Could not read numeric integer argument to '{name}': invalid digit found in string")

def parse_float_arg(name, value):
    try:
        return float(value)
    except:
        error_runtime(f"Could not read numeric argument to '{name}': invalid digit found in string")

def format_time(seconds, unit=None):
    # unit: None auto, or "microsecond","millisecond","second","s","ms","us"
    if unit is None or unit == "auto":
        # auto based on magnitude: <0.001 => us, <1 => ms, else s
        if seconds < 0.001:
            unit = "microsecond"
        elif seconds < 1.0:
            unit = "millisecond"
        else:
            unit = "second"
    # normalize
    if unit in ("microsecond","microseconds","us","µs"):
        val = seconds*1e6
        return f"{val:.1f} µs"
    elif unit in ("millisecond","milliseconds","ms"):
        val = seconds*1e3
        return f"{val:.1f} ms"
    elif unit in ("second","seconds","s"):
        val = seconds
        return f"{val:.3f} s"
    else:
        val = seconds*1e3
        return f"{val:.1f} ms"

def format_time_for_export(seconds, unit):
    # returns formatted value without unit, for table cell: e.g., "20.7" or "20.7 ± 0.1"
    # unit is chosen for export table
    if unit in ("microsecond","us","µs"):
        val = seconds*1e6
        return f"{val:.1f}"
    elif unit in ("millisecond","ms"):
        val = seconds*1e3
        return f"{val:.1f}"
    elif unit in ("second","s"):
        val = seconds
        return f"{val:.3f}"
    else:
        val = seconds*1e3
        return f"{val:.1f}"

def choose_export_unit(means, time_unit_opt):
    if time_unit_opt is not None:
        if time_unit_opt == "microsecond":
            return "microsecond", "µs"
        if time_unit_opt == "millisecond":
            return "millisecond", "ms"
        if time_unit_opt == "second":
            return "second", "s"
    # auto
    min_mean = min(means) if means else 0
    if min_mean < 0.001:
        return "microsecond", "µs"
    elif min_mean < 1.0:
        return "millisecond", "ms"
    else:
        return "second", "s"

def main():
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    # quick help/version
    # we need to parse but first handle --help/-h and --version/-V before errors? hyperfine does clap handling: --help prints help even if missing commands.
    # So we should check for help/version early.
    # However if help is present, we just print and exit 0 regardless of other errors?
    # Implement: if any -h/--help in argv, print help and exit 0.
    # Similarly -V/--version.
    for arg in argv:
        if arg in ("-h","--help"):
            sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
            # Ensure ends with newline
            if not HELP_TEXT.endswith("\n"):
                sys.stdout.write("\n")
            sys.exit(0)
        if arg in ("-V","--version"):
            sys.stdout.write(VERSION+"\n")
            sys.exit(0)

    # Now parse
    warmup = None
    min_runs = None
    max_runs = None
    runs = None
    setup_cmds = [] # single maybe
    reference = None
    reference_name = None
    prepare_cmds = []
    conclude_cmds = []
    cleanup_cmds = []
    parameter_scans = [] # list of dict var,min,max
    parameter_step_size = None
    parameter_lists = [] # list of dict var,values_str
    shell_opt = None
    shell_is_none_flag = False
    ignore_failure = None # None not set, "" means set without value, else string value
    ignore_failure_set = False
    style = "auto"
    sort = "auto"
    time_unit = None
    export_asciidoc = None
    export_csv = None
    export_json = None
    export_markdown = None
    export_orgmode = None
    show_output = False
    output_where = []
    input_where = None
    command_names = []
    commands = []

    # track which options have been set to detect duplicates where disallowed
    seen_warmup = False
    seen_min_runs = False
    seen_max_runs = False
    seen_runs = False
    seen_setup = False
    seen_reference = False
    seen_reference_name = False
    seen_parameter_step_size = False
    seen_shell = False
    seen_style = False
    seen_sort = False
    seen_time_unit = False
    seen_export_asciidoc = False
    seen_export_csv = False
    seen_export_json = False
    seen_export_markdown = False
    seen_export_orgmode = False
    seen_input = False

    i=0
    n=len(argv)
    # helper to get next value
    def require_value(opt_name, idx):
        if idx >= n:
            error_clap(f"a value is required for '{opt_name} <FILE>' but none was supplied")
        return argv[idx]

    while i < n:
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--":
            # rest are commands
            commands.extend(argv[i+1:])
            break
        elif arg in ("-w","--warmup"):
            if seen_warmup:
                error_clap("the argument '--warmup <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            val = require_value("--warmup", i+1)
            i+=1
            # parse later
            warmup = val
            seen_warmup=True
        elif arg.startswith("--warmup="):
            if seen_warmup:
                error_clap("the argument '--warmup <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            warmup = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_warmup=True
        elif arg.startswith("-w"):
            # Could be -w5 or -w 5? But clap usually allows -w NUM ; we treat -w as requiring value, but if argument like "-w5", we need handle.
            if arg == "-w":
                # handled above
                pass
            else:
                # e.g., -w3
                if seen_warmup:
                    error_clap("the argument '--warmup <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
                warmup = arg[2:]
                if warmup == "":
                    val = require_value("--warmup", i+1)
                    i+=1
                    warmup = val
                seen_warmup=True
        elif arg in ("-m","--min-runs"):
            if seen_min_runs:
                error_clap("the argument '--min-runs <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            val = require_value("--min-runs", i+1)
            i+=1
            min_runs = val
            seen_min_runs=True
        elif arg.startswith("--min-runs="):
            if seen_min_runs:
                error_clap("the argument '--min-runs <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            min_runs = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_min_runs=True
        elif arg in ("-M","--max-runs"):
            if seen_max_runs:
                error_clap("the argument '--max-runs <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            val = require_value("--max-runs", i+1)
            i+=1
            max_runs = val
            seen_max_runs=True
        elif arg.startswith("--max-runs="):
            if seen_max_runs:
                error_clap("the argument '--max-runs <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            max_runs = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_max_runs=True
        elif arg in ("-r","--runs"):
            if seen_runs:
                error_clap("the argument '--runs <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            val = require_value("--runs", i+1)
            i+=1
            runs = val
            seen_runs=True
        elif arg.startswith("--runs="):
            if seen_runs:
                error_clap("the argument '--runs <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            runs = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_runs=True
        elif arg in ("-s","--setup"):
            val = require_value("--setup", i+1)
            i+=1
            setup_cmds.append(val)
            seen_setup=True
        elif arg.startswith("--setup="):
            setup_cmds.append(arg.split("=",1)[1])
            seen_setup=True
        elif arg == "--reference":
            if seen_reference:
                error_clap("the argument '--reference <CMD>' cannot be used multiple times")
            val = require_value("--reference", i+1)
            i+=1
            reference = val
            seen_reference=True
        elif arg.startswith("--reference="):
            if seen_reference:
                error_clap("the argument '--reference <CMD>' cannot be used multiple times")
            reference = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_reference=True
        elif arg == "--reference-name":
            if seen_reference_name:
                error_clap("the argument '--reference-name <CMD>' cannot be used multiple times")
            val = require_value("--reference-name", i+1)
            i+=1
            reference_name = val
            seen_reference_name=True
        elif arg.startswith("--reference-name="):
            if seen_reference_name:
                error_clap("the argument '--reference-name <CMD>' cannot be used multiple times")
            reference_name = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_reference_name=True
        elif arg in ("-p","--prepare"):
            val = require_value("--prepare", i+1)
            i+=1
            prepare_cmds.append(val)
        elif arg.startswith("--prepare="):
            prepare_cmds.append(arg.split("=",1)[1])
        elif arg.startswith("-p"):
            # -pval?
            if arg == "-p":
                pass
            else:
                prepare_cmds.append(arg[2:])
        elif arg in ("-C","--conclude"):
            val = require_value("--conclude", i+1)
            i+=1
            conclude_cmds.append(val)
        elif arg.startswith("--conclude="):
            conclude_cmds.append(arg.split("=",1)[1])
        elif arg in ("-c","--cleanup"):
            val = require_value("--cleanup", i+1)
            i+=1
            cleanup_cmds.append(val)
        elif arg.startswith("--cleanup="):
            cleanup_cmds.append(arg.split("=",1)[1])
        elif arg in ("-P","--parameter-scan"):
            # needs 3 values
            if i+3 >= n:
                error_clap("a value is required for '--parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>' but none was supplied")
            var = argv[i+1]; minv = argv[i+2]; maxv = argv[i+3]
            # Check that var doesn't look like an option? hyperfine would treat next args as values even if they start with -; but we assume correct.
            parameter_scans.append((var, minv, maxv))
            i+=3
        elif arg.startswith("--parameter-scan="):
            # Could be --parameter-scan=VAR? but we need 3 values, so treat as error
            error_clap("a value is required for '--parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>' but none was supplied")
        elif arg in ("-D","--parameter-step-size"):
            if seen_parameter_step_size:
                error_clap("the argument '--parameter-step-size <DELTA>' cannot be used multiple times")
            val = require_value("--parameter-step-size", i+1)
            i+=1
            parameter_step_size = val
            seen_parameter_step_size=True
        elif arg.startswith("--parameter-step-size="):
            if seen_parameter_step_size:
                error_clap("the argument '--parameter-step-size <DELTA>' cannot be used multiple times")
            parameter_step_size = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_parameter_step_size=True
        elif arg.startswith("-D"):
            if seen_parameter_step_size:
                error_clap("the argument '--parameter-step-size <DELTA>' cannot be used multiple times")
            if arg == "-D":
                val = require_value("--parameter-step-size", i+1)
                i+=1
                parameter_step_size = val
            else:
                parameter_step_size = arg[2:]
            seen_parameter_step_size=True
        elif arg in ("-L","--parameter-list"):
            if i+2 >= n:
                error_clap("a value is required for '--parameter-list <VAR> <VALUES>' but none was supplied")
            var = argv[i+1]; values = argv[i+2]
            parameter_lists.append((var, values))
            i+=2
        elif arg.startswith("--parameter-list="):
            error_clap("a value is required for '--parameter-list <VAR> <VALUES>' but none was supplied")
        elif arg in ("-S","--shell"):
            if seen_shell:
                # hyperfine maybe allows multiple? But we treat as only once? Original allows once. We'll error if duplicate?
                # For --shell, clap would error on multiple uses? But not tested. We'll allow only once.
                error_clap("the argument '--shell <SHELL>' cannot be used multiple times")
            val = require_value("--shell", i+1)
            i+=1
            shell_opt = val
            seen_shell=True
        elif arg.startswith("--shell="):
            if seen_shell:
                error_clap("the argument '--shell <SHELL>' cannot be used multiple times")
            shell_opt = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_shell=True
        elif arg == "-N":
            shell_opt = "none"
            shell_is_none_flag = True
            seen_shell=True
        elif arg in ("-i","--ignore-failure"):
            # optional value, may be next arg if not starting with -
            # Could be --ignore-failure=val or -i val
            # Check if next arg exists and doesn't look like option but could be value like "1,2" or "all-non-zero"
            # If arg is -i and next is value not starting with -, treat as value. If next is None or starts with -, value is None (meaning all).
            # But also --ignore-failure without = should capture next as optional.
            # We support forms:
            #   --ignore-failure
            #   --ignore-failure=all-non-zero
            #   --ignore-failure=1,2
            #   -i
            #   -i all-non-zero
            #   -i 1,2
            # For -i, we need to peek.
            if arg == "--ignore-failure" or arg == "-i":
                # peek next
                if i+1 < n and not argv[i+1].startswith("-"):
                    # but could be a command? In hyperfine, --ignore-failure is not required to have command before, but if next token is command, we shouldn't consume it as value?
                    # However hyperfine's ignore-failure with optional value: if provided, it's value; otherwise command follows. Heuristic: if next token contains comma or is all-non-zero or is numeric, treat as value.
                    nxt = argv[i+1]
                    # check if it looks like mode/value
                    if nxt in ("all-non-zero",) or re.match(r'^[0-9,]+$', nxt):
                        ignore_failure = nxt
                        ignore_failure_set=True
                        i+=1
                    else:
                        # ambiguous: if next token is something like "echo", that's a command, not ignore value
                        # We'll treat no value
                        ignore_failure = ""  # meaning all
                        ignore_failure_set=True
                else:
                    ignore_failure = ""
                    ignore_failure_set=True
            else:
                # unreachable
                pass
        elif arg.startswith("--ignore-failure="):
            ignore_failure = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            ignore_failure_set=True
        elif arg.startswith("-i"):
            # -iVALUE? like -i1,2
            if arg == "-i":
                pass # handled above
            else:
                # e.g., -i1,2 or -iall-non-zero
                ignore_failure = arg[2:]
                ignore_failure_set=True
        elif arg == "--style":
            if seen_style:
                error_clap("the argument '--style <TYPE>' cannot be used multiple times")
            val = require_value("--style", i+1)
            i+=1
            style = val
            seen_style=True
        elif arg.startswith("--style="):
            if seen_style:
                error_clap("the argument '--style <TYPE>' cannot be used multiple times")
            style = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_style=True
        elif arg == "--sort":
            if seen_sort:
                error_clap("the argument '--sort <METHOD>' cannot be used multiple times")
            val = require_value("--sort", i+1)
            i+=1
            sort = val
            seen_sort=True
        elif arg.startswith("--sort="):
            if seen_sort:
                error_clap("the argument '--sort <METHOD>' cannot be used multiple times")
            sort = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_sort=True
        elif arg in ("-u","--time-unit"):
            if seen_time_unit:
                error_clap("the argument '--time-unit <UNIT>' cannot be used multiple times")
            val = require_value("--time-unit", i+1)
            i+=1
            time_unit = val
            seen_time_unit=True
        elif arg.startswith("--time-unit="):
            if seen_time_unit:
                error_clap("the argument '--time-unit <UNIT>' cannot be used multiple times")
            time_unit = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_time_unit=True
        elif arg.startswith("-u"):
            if arg == "-u":
                pass
            else:
                if seen_time_unit:
                    error_clap("the argument '--time-unit <UNIT>' cannot be used multiple times")
                time_unit = arg[2:]
                seen_time_unit=True
        elif arg == "--export-asciidoc":
            val = require_value("--export-asciidoc", i+1)
            i+=1
            export_asciidoc = val
            seen_export_asciidoc=True
        elif arg.startswith("--export-asciidoc="):
            export_asciidoc = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_export_asciidoc=True
        elif arg == "--export-csv":
            val = require_value("--export-csv", i+1)
            i+=1
            export_csv = val
            seen_export_csv=True
        elif arg.startswith("--export-csv="):
            export_csv = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_export_csv=True
        elif arg == "--export-json":
            val = require_value("--export-json", i+1)
            i+=1
            export_json = val
            seen_export_json=True
        elif arg.startswith("--export-json="):
            export_json = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_export_json=True
        elif arg == "--export-markdown":
            val = require_value("--export-markdown", i+1)
            i+=1
            export_markdown = val
            seen_export_markdown=True
        elif arg.startswith("--export-markdown="):
            export_markdown = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_export_markdown=True
        elif arg == "--export-orgmode":
            val = require_value("--export-orgmode", i+1)
            i+=1
            export_orgmode = val
            seen_export_orgmode=True
        elif arg.startswith("--export-orgmode="):
            export_orgmode = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_export_orgmode=True
        elif arg == "--show-output":
            show_output = True
        elif arg == "--output":
            val = require_value("--output", i+1)
            i+=1
            output_where.append(val)
        elif arg.startswith("--output="):
            output_where.append(arg.split("=",1)[1])
        elif arg == "--input":
            if seen_input:
                error_clap("the argument '--input <WHERE>' cannot be used multiple times")
            val = require_value("--input", i+1)
            i+=1
            input_where = val
            seen_input=True
        elif arg.startswith("--input="):
            if seen_input:
                error_clap("the argument '--input <WHERE>' cannot be used multiple times")
            input_where = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_input=True
        elif arg in ("-n","--command-name"):
            val = require_value("--command-name", i+1)
            i+=1
            command_names.append(val)
        elif arg.startswith("--command-name="):
            command_names.append(arg.split("=",1)[1])
        elif arg.startswith("-n"):
            if arg == "-n":
                pass
            else:
                command_names.append(arg[2:])
        elif arg == "-h" or arg == "--help":
            # already handled
            pass
        elif arg == "-V" or arg == "--version":
            pass
        elif arg.startswith("-"):
            # unknown flag
            error_clap(f"unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{arg}' as a value, use '-- {arg}'")
        else:
            # positional command
            commands.append(arg)
        i+=1

    # Validation
    # --parameter-step-size requires --parameter-scan
    if parameter_step_size is not None and not parameter_scans:
        error_clap("the following required arguments were not provided:\n  --parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>", usage="executable --parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX> --parameter-step-size <DELTA> <command>...")
        # usage with scan/step
    # --reference-name requires --reference
    if reference_name is not None and reference is None:
        error_clap("the following required arguments were not provided:\n  --reference <CMD>", usage="executable --reference <CMD> --reference-name <CMD> <command>...")
    # --style with --show-output conflict
    if show_output and style != "auto":
        # hyperfine errors when style explicitly != auto and show_output. But default style is auto, so if user didn't set style, no error. If they set style to auto? That's still explicit? But we track seen_style
        if seen_style:
            error_clap("the argument '--style <TYPE>' cannot be used with '--show-output'", usage="executable --runs <NUM> --warmup <NUM> --prepare <CMD> --setup <CMD> --cleanup <CMD> --conclude <CMD> --style <TYPE> <command>...")

    # --runs conflicts with --min-runs and --max-runs
    if runs is not None and min_runs is not None:
        error_clap("the argument '--runs <NUM>' cannot be used with '--min-runs <NUM>'", usage="executable --runs <NUM> <command>...")
    if runs is not None and max_runs is not None:
        error_clap("the argument '--runs <NUM>' cannot be used with '--max-runs <NUM>'", usage="executable --runs <NUM> <command>...")

    # Validate enums
    if style not in ("auto","basic","full","nocolor","color","none"):
        error_clap(f"invalid value '{style}' for '--style <TYPE>'\n  [possible values: auto, basic, full, nocolor, color, none]")
    if sort not in ("auto","command","mean-time"):
        error_clap(f"invalid value '{sort}' for '--sort <METHOD>'\n  [possible values: auto, command, mean-time]")
    if time_unit is not None and time_unit not in ("microsecond","millisecond","second"):
        error_clap(f"invalid value '{time_unit}' for '--time-unit <UNIT>'\n  [possible values: microsecond, millisecond, second]")

    # Validate numeric args
    warmup_val = 0
    if warmup is not None:
        warmup_val = parse_int_arg("--warmup", warmup)
        if warmup_val < 0:
            error_clap("unexpected argument '-1' found\n\n  tip: to pass '-1' as a value, use '-- -1'")
    else:
        warmup_val = 0

    min_runs_val = 10
    if min_runs is not None:
        min_runs_val = parse_int_arg("--min-runs", min_runs)
    max_runs_val = None
    if max_runs is not None:
        max_runs_val = parse_int_arg("--max-runs", max_runs)
    runs_val = None
    if runs is not None:

        val = seconds*1e6
        return f"{val:.1f} µs"
    elif unit in ("millisecond","milliseconds","ms"):
        val = seconds*1e3
        return f"{val:.1f} ms"
    elif unit in ("second","seconds","s"):
        val = seconds
        return f"{val:.3f} s"
    else:
        val = seconds*1e3
        return f"{val:.1f} ms"

def format_time_for_export(seconds, unit):
    # returns formatted value without unit, for table cell: e.g., "20.7" or "20.7 ± 0.1"
    # unit is chosen for export table
    if unit in ("microsecond","us","µs"):
        val = seconds*1e6
        return f"{val:.1f}"
    elif unit in ("millisecond","ms"):
        val = seconds*1e3
        return f"{val:.1f}"
    elif unit in ("second","s"):
        val = seconds
        return f"{val:.3f}"
    else:
        val = seconds*1e3
        return f"{val:.1f}"

def choose_export_unit(means, time_unit_opt):
    if time_unit_opt is not None:
        if time_unit_opt == "microsecond":
            return "microsecond", "µs"
        if time_unit_opt == "millisecond":
            return "millisecond", "ms"
        if time_unit_opt == "second":
            return "second", "s"
    # auto
    min_mean = min(means) if means else 0
    if min_mean < 0.001:
        return "microsecond", "µs"
    elif min_mean < 1.0:
        return "millisecond", "ms"
    else:
        return "second", "s"

          echo test". The latter is only available if the shell is not
          explicitly disabled via '--shell=none'. If multiple commands are
          given, hyperfine will show a comparison of the respective runtimes.

Options:
  -w, --warmup <NUM>
          Perform NUM warmup runs before the actual benchmark. This can be used
          to fill (disk) caches for I/O-heavy programs.
  -m, --min-runs <NUM>
          Perform at least NUM runs for each command (default: 10).
  -M, --max-runs <NUM>
          Perform at most NUM runs for each command. By default, there is no
          limit.
  -r, --runs <NUM>
          Perform exactly NUM runs for each command. If this option is not
          specified, hyperfine automatically determines the number of runs.
  -s, --setup <CMD>
          Execute CMD before each set of timing runs. This is useful for
          compiling your software with the provided parameters, or to do any
          other work that should happen once before a series of benchmark runs,
          not every time as would happen with the --prepare option.
      --reference <CMD>
          The reference command for the relative comparison of results. If this
          is unset, results are compared with the fastest command as reference.
      --reference-name <CMD>
          Give a meaningful name to the reference command.
  -p, --prepare <CMD>
          Execute CMD before each timing run. This is useful for clearing disk
          caches, for example.
          The --prepare option can be specified once for all commands or
          multiple times, once for each command. In the latter case, each
          preparation command will be run prior to the corresponding benchmark
          command.
  -C, --conclude <CMD>
          Execute CMD after each timing run. This is useful for killing
          long-running processes started (e.g. a web server started in
          --prepare), for example.
          The --conclude option can be specified once for all commands or
          multiple times, once for each command. In the latter case, each
          conclude command will be run after the corresponding benchmark
          command.
  -c, --cleanup <CMD>
          Execute CMD after the completion of all benchmarking runs for each
          individual command to be benchmarked. This is useful if the commands
          to be benchmarked produce artifacts that need to be cleaned up.
  -P, --parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>
          Perform benchmark runs for each value in the range MIN..MAX. Replaces
          the string '{VAR}' in each command by the current parameter value.
          
            Example:  hyperfine -P threads 1 8 'make -j {threads}'
          
          This performs benchmarks for 'make -j 1', 'make -j 2', …, 'make -j 8'.
          
          To have the value increase following different patterns, use shell
          arithmetics.
          
            Example: hyperfine -P size 0 3 'sleep $((2**{size}))'
          
          This performs benchmarks for 'sleep 1', 'sleep 2', 'sleep 4', …
          The exact syntax may vary depending on your shell and OS.
  -D, --parameter-step-size <DELTA>
          This argument requires --parameter-scan to be specified as well.
          Traverse the range MIN..MAX in steps of DELTA.
          
            Example:  hyperfine -P delay 0.3 0.7 -D 0.2 'sleep {delay}'
          
          This performs benchmarks for 'sleep 0.3', 'sleep 0.5' and 'sleep 0.7'.
  -L, --parameter-list <VAR> <VALUES>
          Perform benchmark runs for each value in the comma-separated list
          VALUES. Replaces the string '{VAR}' in each command by the current
          parameter value.
          
          Example:  hyperfine -L compiler gcc,clang '{compiler} -O2 main.cpp'
          
          This performs benchmarks for 'gcc -O2 main.cpp' and 'clang -O2
          main.cpp'.
          
          The option can be specified multiple times to run benchmarks for all
          possible parameter combinations.
  -S, --shell <SHELL>
          Set the shell to use for executing benchmarked commands. This can be
          the name or the path to the shell executable, or a full command line
          like "bash --norc". It can also be set to "default" to explicitly
          select the default shell on this platform. Finally, this can also be
          set to "none" to disable the shell. In this case, commands will be
          executed directly. They can still have arguments, but more complex
          things like "sleep 0.1; sleep 0.2" are not possible without a shell.
  -N
          An alias for '--shell=none'.
  -i, --ignore-failure[=<MODE>]
          Ignore failures of the benchmarked programs. Without a value or with
          'all-non-zero', all non-zero exit codes are ignored. You can also
          provide a comma-separated list of exit codes to ignore (e.g.,
          --ignore-failure=1,2).
      --style <TYPE>
          Set output style type (default: auto). Set this to 'basic' to disable
          output coloring and interactive elements. Set it to 'full' to enable
          all effects even if no interactive terminal was detected. Set this to
          'nocolor' to keep the interactive output without any colors. Set this
          to 'color' to keep the colors without any interactive output. Set this
          to 'none' to disable all the output of the tool.
      --sort <METHOD>
          Specify the sort order of the speed comparison summary and the
          exported tables for markup formats (Markdown, AsciiDoc, org-mode):
            * 'auto' (default): the speed comparison will be ordered by time and
              the markup tables will be ordered by command (input order).
            * 'command': order benchmarks in the way they were specified
            * 'mean-time': order benchmarks by mean runtime
  -u, --time-unit <UNIT>
          Set the time unit to be used. Possible values: microsecond,
          millisecond, second. If the option is not given, the time unit is
          determined automatically. This option affects the standard output as
          well as all export formats except for CSV and JSON.
      --export-asciidoc <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as an AsciiDoc table to the given
          FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit
          option.
      --export-csv <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as CSV to the given FILE. If you
          need the timing results for each individual run, use the JSON export
          format. The output time unit is always seconds.
      --export-json <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics and timings of individual runs as
          JSON to the given FILE. The output time unit is always seconds
      --export-markdown <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as a Markdown table to the given
          FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit
          option.
      --export-orgmode <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as an Emacs org-mode table to the
          given FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit
          option.
      --show-output
          Print the stdout and stderr of the benchmark instead of suppressing
          it. This will increase the time it takes for benchmarks to run, so it
          should only be used for debugging purposes or when trying to benchmark
          output speed.
      --output <WHERE>
          Control where the output of the benchmark is redirected. Note that
          some programs like 'grep' detect when standard output is /dev/null and
          apply certain optimizations. To avoid that, consider using
          '--output=pipe'.
          
          <WHERE> can be:
          
            null:     Redirect output to /dev/null (the default).
          
            pipe:     Feed the output through a pipe before discarding it.
          
            inherit:  Don't redirect the output at all (same as
            '--show-output').
          
            <FILE>:   Write the output to the given file.
          
          This option can be specified once for all commands or multiple times,
          once for each command. Note: If you want to log the output of each and
          every iteration, you can use a shell redirection and the
          '$HYPERFINE_ITERATION' environment variable:
              hyperfine 'my-command > output-${HYPERFINE_ITERATION}.log'
      --input <WHERE>
          Control where the input of the benchmark comes from.
          
          <WHERE> can be:
          
            null:     Read from /dev/null (the default).
          
            <FILE>:   Read the input from the given file.
  -n, --command-name <NAME>
          Give a meaningful name to a command. This can be specified multiple
          times if several commands are benchmarked.
  -h, --help
          Print help
  -V, --version
          Print version
"""
VERSION = "hyperfine 1.20.0"

def eprint(msg):
    sys.stderr.write(msg + ("\n" if not msg.endswith("\n") else ""))

def error_clap(msg, usage="executable [OPTIONS] <command>..."):
    sys.stderr.write(f"error: {msg}\n\nUsage: {usage}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
    sys.exit(2)

def error_runtime(msg):
    sys.stderr.write(f"Error: {msg}\n")
    sys.exit(1)

def parse_int_arg(name, value):
    try:
        # allow negative? but we check later
        return int(value, 10)
    except:
        error_runtime(f"Could not read numeric integer argument to '{name}': invalid digit found in string")

def format_time(seconds, unit=None):
    # choose unit if None
    if unit is None or unit == "auto":
        if seconds < 0.001:
            unit = "microsecond"
        elif seconds < 1.0:
            unit = "millisecond"
        else:
            unit = "second"
    if unit in ("microsecond","microseconds","us","µs"):
        v = seconds*1e6
        return f"{v:.1f} µs"
    elif unit in ("millisecond","milliseconds","ms"):
        v = seconds*1e3
        return f"{v:.1f} ms"
    elif unit in ("second","seconds","s"):
        v = seconds
        return f"{v:.3f} s"
    else:
        v = seconds*1e3
        return f"{v:.1f} ms"

def format_time_value(seconds, unit):
    if unit == "microsecond":
        return f"{seconds*1e6:.1f}"
    elif unit == "millisecond":
        return f"{seconds*1e3:.1f}"
    elif unit == "second":
        return f"{seconds:.3f}"
    else:
        return f"{seconds*1e3:.1f}"

def choose_unit_for_export(means, time_unit_opt):
    if time_unit_opt is not None:
        if time_unit_opt == "microsecond":
            return "microsecond", "µs"
        elif time_unit_opt == "millisecond":
            return "millisecond", "ms"
        elif time_unit_opt == "second":
            return "second", "s"
    # auto based on minimum mean
    m = min(means) if means else 0
    if m < 0.001:
        return "microsecond", "µs"
    elif m < 1.0:
        return "millisecond", "ms"
    else:
        return "second", "s"

def main():
    argv = sys.argv[1:]

    # early help/version
    for a in argv:
        if a in ("-h","--help"):
            sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
            if not HELP_TEXT.endswith("\n"):
                sys.stdout.write("\n")
            sys.exit(0)
        if a in ("-V","--version"):
            sys.stdout.write(VERSION+"\n")
            sys.exit(0)

    # parsing state
    warmup = None
    min_runs = None
    max_runs = None
    runs = None
    setup_cmds = []
    reference = None
    reference_name = None
    prepare_cmds = []
    conclude_cmds = []
    cleanup_cmds = []
    param_scans = []  # list of (var, min, max)
    param_step = None
    param_lists = []  # list of (var, values_str)
    shell_opt = None
    shell_is_none = False
    ignore_failure = None
    ignore_set = set()
    ignore_all = False
    ignore_set_flag = False
    style = "auto"
    sort = "auto"
    time_unit = None
    export_asciidoc = None
    export_csv = None
    export_json = None
    export_markdown = None
    export_orgmode = None
    show_output = False
    output_where = []
    input_where = None
    command_names = []
    commands = []

    seen_warmup = False
    seen_min = False
    seen_max = False
    seen_runs = False
    seen_shell = False
    seen_style = False
    seen_sort = False
    seen_time_unit = False
    seen_step = False
    seen_ref = False
    seen_ref_name = False
    seen_input = False

    i=0
    n=len(argv)
    def require(opt, idx):
        if idx >= n:
            error_clap(f"a value is required for '{opt} <FILE>' but none was supplied")
        return argv[idx]

    while i < n:
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--":
            commands.extend(argv[i+1:])
            break
        elif arg in ("-w","--warmup"):
            if seen_warmup:
                error_clap("the argument '--warmup <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            v = require("--warmup", i+1)
            i+=1
            warmup = v
            seen_warmup=True
        elif arg.startswith("--warmup="):
            if seen_warmup:
                error_clap("the argument '--warmup <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            warmup = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_warmup=True
        elif arg.startswith("-w") and arg != "-w":
            if seen_warmup:
                error_clap("the argument '--warmup <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            # -w3 or -w=3?
            rest = arg[2:]
            if rest.startswith("="):
                rest = rest[1:]
            if rest == "":
                v = require("--warmup", i+1)
                i+=1
                warmup = v
            else:
                warmup = rest
            seen_warmup=True
        elif arg in ("-m","--min-runs"):
            if seen_min:
                error_clap("the argument '--min-runs <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            v = require("--min-runs", i+1)
            i+=1
            min_runs = v
            seen_min=True
        elif arg.startswith("--min-runs="):
            if seen_min:
                error_clap("the argument '--min-runs <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            min_runs = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_min=True
        elif arg in ("-M","--max-runs"):
            if seen_max:
                error_clap("the argument '--max-runs <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            v = require("--max-runs", i+1)
            i+=1
            max_runs = v
            seen_max=True
        elif arg.startswith("--max-runs="):
            if seen_max:
                error_clap("the argument '--max-runs <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            max_runs = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_max=True
        elif arg in ("-r","--runs"):
            if seen_runs:
                error_clap("the argument '--runs <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            v = require("--runs", i+1)
            i+=1
            runs = v
            seen_runs=True
        elif arg.startswith("--runs="):
            if seen_runs:
                error_clap("the argument '--runs <NUM>' cannot be used multiple times")
            runs = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_runs=True
        elif arg in ("-s","--setup"):
            v = require("--setup", i+1)
            i+=1
            setup_cmds.append(v)
        elif arg.startswith("--setup="):
            setup_cmds.append(arg.split("=",1)[1])
        elif arg == "--reference":
            if seen_ref:
                error_clap("the argument '--reference <CMD>' cannot be used multiple times")
            v = require("--reference", i+1)
            i+=1
            reference = v
            seen_ref=True
        elif arg.startswith("--reference="):
            if seen_ref:
                error_clap("the argument '--reference <CMD>' cannot be used multiple times")
            reference = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_ref=True
        elif arg == "--reference-name":
            if seen_ref_name:
                error_clap("the argument '--reference-name <CMD>' cannot be used multiple times")
            v = require("--reference-name", i+1)
            i+=1
            reference_name = v
            seen_ref_name=True
        elif arg.startswith("--reference-name="):
            if seen_ref_name:
                error_clap("the argument '--reference-name <CMD>' cannot be used multiple times")
            reference_name = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_ref_name=True
        elif arg in ("-p","--prepare"):
            v = require("--prepare", i+1)
            i+=1
            prepare_cmds.append(v)
        elif arg.startswith("--prepare="):
            prepare_cmds.append(arg.split("=",1)[1])
        elif arg.startswith("-p") and arg != "-p":
            prepare_cmds.append(arg[2:])
        elif arg in ("-C","--conclude"):
            v = require("--conclude", i+1)
            i+=1
            conclude_cmds.append(v)
        elif arg.startswith("--conclude="):
            conclude_cmds.append(arg.split("=",1)[1])
        elif arg in ("-c","--cleanup"):
            v = require("--cleanup", i+1)
            i+=1
            cleanup_cmds.append(v)
        elif arg.startswith("--cleanup="):
            cleanup_cmds.append(arg.split("=",1)[1])
        elif arg in ("-P","--parameter-scan"):
            if i+3 >= n:
                error_clap("a value is required for '--parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>' but none was supplied")
            var = argv[i+1]; mn = argv[i+2]; mx = argv[i+3]
            param_scans.append((var,mn,mx))
            i+=3
        elif arg.startswith("--parameter-scan="):
            error_clap("a value is required for '--parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>' but none was supplied")
        elif arg in ("-D","--parameter-step-size"):
            if seen_step:
                error_clap("the argument '--parameter-step-size <DELTA>' cannot be used multiple times")
            v = require("--parameter-step-size", i+1)
            i+=1
            param_step = v
            seen_step=True
        elif arg.startswith("--parameter-step-size="):
            if seen_step:
                error_clap("the argument '--parameter-step-size <DELTA>' cannot be used multiple times")
            param_step = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_step=True
        elif arg.startswith("-D") and arg != "-D":
            if seen_step:
                error_clap("the argument '--parameter-step-size <DELTA>' cannot be used multiple times")
            param_step = arg[2:]
            seen_step=True
        elif arg in ("-L","--parameter-list"):
            if i+2 >= n:
                error_clap("a value is required for '--parameter-list <VAR> <VALUES>' but none was supplied")
            var = argv[i+1]; vals = argv[i+2]
            param_lists.append((var, vals))
            i+=2
        elif arg.startswith("--parameter-list="):
            error_clap("a value is required for '--parameter-list <VAR> <VALUES>' but none was supplied")
        elif arg in ("-S","--shell"):
            if seen_shell:
                error_clap("the argument '--shell <SHELL>' cannot be used multiple times")
            v = require("--shell", i+1)
            i+=1
            shell_opt = v
            seen_shell=True
        elif arg.startswith("--shell="):
            if seen_shell:
                error_clap("the argument '--shell <SHELL>' cannot be used multiple times")
            shell_opt = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_shell=True
        elif arg == "-N":
            shell_opt = "none"
            shell_is_none = True
            seen_shell=True
        elif arg in ("-i","--ignore-failure"):
            # optional value
            nxt = argv[i+1] if i+1 < n else None
            if nxt is not None and not nxt.startswith("-") and (nxt == "all-non-zero" or re.match(r'^[0-9,]+$', nxt)):
                ignore_failure = nxt
                ignore_set_flag = True
                i+=1
            else:
                # check if arg has =? Already handled --ignore-failure= above
                ignore_failure = ""
                ignore_set_flag = True
        elif arg.startswith("--ignore-failure="):
            ignore_failure = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            ignore_set_flag = True
        elif arg.startswith("-i") and arg != "-i":
            ignore_failure = arg[2:]
            ignore_set_flag = True
        elif arg == "--style":
            if seen_style:
                error_clap("the argument '--style <TYPE>' cannot be used multiple times")
            v = require("--style", i+1)
            i+=1
            style = v
            seen_style=True
        elif arg.startswith("--style="):
            if seen_style:
                error_clap("the argument '--style <TYPE>' cannot be used multiple times")
            style = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_style=True
        elif arg == "--sort":
            if seen_sort:
                error_clap("the argument '--sort <METHOD>' cannot be used multiple times")
            v = require("--sort", i+1)
            i+=1
            sort = v
            seen_sort=True
        elif arg.startswith("--sort="):
            if seen_sort:
                error_clap("the argument '--sort <METHOD>' cannot be used multiple times")
            sort = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_sort=True
        elif arg in ("-u","--time-unit"):
            if seen_time_unit:
                error_clap("the argument '--time-unit <UNIT>' cannot be used multiple times")
            v = require("--time-unit", i+1)
            i+=1
            time_unit = v
            seen_time_unit=True
        elif arg.startswith("--time-unit="):
            if seen_time_unit:
                error_clap("the argument '--time-unit <UNIT>' cannot be used multiple times")
            time_unit = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_time_unit=True
        elif arg.startswith("-u") and arg != "-u":
            if seen_time_unit:
                error_clap("the argument '--time-unit <UNIT>' cannot be used multiple times")
            time_unit = arg[2:]
            seen_time_unit=True
        elif arg == "--export-asciidoc":
            v = require("--export-asciidoc", i+1)
            i+=1
            export_asciidoc = v
        elif arg.startswith("--export-asciidoc="):
            export_asciidoc = arg.split("=",1)[1]
        elif arg == "--export-csv":
            v = require("--export-csv", i+1)
            i+=1
            export_csv = v
        elif arg.startswith("--export-csv="):
            export_csv = arg.split("=",1)[1]
        elif arg == "--export-json":
            v = require("--export-json", i+1)
            i+=1
            export_json = v
        elif arg.startswith("--export-json="):
            export_json = arg.split("=",1)[1]
        elif arg == "--export-markdown":
            v = require("--export-markdown", i+1)
            i+=1
            export_markdown = v
        elif arg.startswith("--export-markdown="):
            export_markdown = arg.split("=",1)[1]
        elif arg == "--export-orgmode":
            v = require("--export-orgmode", i+1)
            i+=1
            export_orgmode = v
        elif arg.startswith("--export-orgmode="):
            export_orgmode = arg.split("=",1)[1]
        elif arg == "--show-output":
            show_output = True
        elif arg == "--output":
            v = require("--output", i+1)
            i+=1
            output_where.append(v)
        elif arg.startswith("--output="):
            output_where.append(arg.split("=",1)[1])
        elif arg == "--input":
            if seen_input:
                error_clap("the argument '--input <WHERE>' cannot be used multiple times")
            v = require("--input", i+1)
            i+=1
            input_where = v
            seen_input=True
        elif arg.startswith("--input="):
            if seen_input:
                error_clap("the argument '--input <WHERE>' cannot be used multiple times")
            input_where = arg.split("=",1)[1]
            seen_input=True
        elif arg in ("-n","--command-name"):
            v = require("--command-name", i+1)
            i+=1
            command_names.append(v)
        elif arg.startswith("--command-name="):
            command_names.append(arg.split("=",1)[1])
        elif arg.startswith("-n") and arg != "-n":
            command_names.append(arg[2:])
        elif arg.startswith("-") and arg != "-":
            # unknown
            error_clap(f"unexpected argument '{arg}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{arg}' as a value, use '-- {arg}'")
        else:
            commands.append(arg)
        i+=1

    # validation
    if param_step is not None and not param_scans:
        error_clap("the following required arguments were not provided:\n  --parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>", usage="executable --parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX> --parameter-step-size <DELTA> <command>...")
    if reference_name is not None and reference is None:
        error_clap("the following required arguments were not provided:\n  --reference <CMD>", usage="executable --reference <CMD> --reference-name <CMD> <command>...")
    if show_output and seen_style:
        error_clap("the argument '--style <TYPE>' cannot be used with '--show-output'", usage="executable --runs <NUM> --warmup <NUM> --prepare <CMD> --setup <CMD> --cleanup <CMD> --conclude <CMD> --style <TYPE> <command>...")
    if runs is not None and min_runs is not None:
        error_clap("the argument '--runs <NUM>' cannot be used with '--min-runs <NUM>'", usage="executable --runs <NUM> <command>...")
    if runs is not None and max_runs is not None:
        error_clap("the argument '--runs <NUM>' cannot be used with '--max-runs <NUM>'", usage="executable --runs <NUM> <command>...")
    if style not in ("auto","basic","full","nocolor","color","none"):
        error_clap(f"invalid value '{style}' for '--style <TYPE>'\n  [possible values: auto, basic, full, nocolor, color, none]")
    if sort not in ("auto","command","mean-time"):
        error_clap(f"invalid value '{sort}' for '--sort <METHOD>'\n  [possible values: auto, command, mean-time]")
    if time_unit is not None and time_unit not in ("microsecond","millisecond","second"):
        error_clap(f"invalid value '{time_unit}' for '--time-unit <UNIT>'\n  [possible values: microsecond, millisecond, second]")

    warmup_val = 0
    if warmup is not None:
        warmup_val = parse_int_arg("--warmup", warmup)
        if warmup_val < 0:
            error_clap("unexpected argument '-1' found\n\n  tip: to pass '-1' as a value, use '-- -1'")
    min_runs_val = 10
    if min_runs is not None:
        min_runs_val = parse_int_arg("--min-runs", min_runs)
    max_runs_val = None

            parts = shlex.split(shell_ex)

        start = time.perf_counter()

            if is_pipe:

                st = time.perf_counter()

                en = time.perf_counter()
                after = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
                wall = en - st
                wall = max(0.0, wall - overhead_sec)
                user = after.ru_utime - before.ru_utime
                syst = after.ru_stime - before.ru_stime
                maxrss = after.ru_maxrss * 1024
                ec = proc.returncode

                env_iter = {"HYPERFINE_ITERATION": str(idx)}
                wall,u,s,mem,ec = execute_cmd(cmd, shell_exec, overhead, env_iter, input_file, output_per[b_idx], show_output)
                if ec != 0 and not (ignore_all or ec in ignore_set):
